source: Chen, Gilbert, Grochowski, et al. (2018), 'A genome-wide association study identifies a susceptibility locus for biliary atresia on 2p16.1 within the gene EFEMP1', PLOS Genetics 14(8):e1007532. CC0 license.
note_to_agent: Below is the complete set of analytical results from a genetic association study of biliary atresia (BA), a rare pediatric liver disease. This includes results from two separate patient cohorts and a combined meta-analysis. No interpretation or discussion by the study's authors is included below. Base your answer only on the evidence provided.

significance_thresholds.suggestive_significance: P < 1e-5, defined as an average of one false-positive association per GWAS

evidence_items.description: Discovery cohort: 343 isolated BA patients vs 1,716 controls, European-American ancestry, 1,171,073 markers tested. Top SNP rs10865291, intron 5 of EFEMP1 (chromosome 2p16.1). P = 5.85e-7, odds ratio = 1.56. Minor allele frequency 43% in cases vs 33% in controls. This does not reach the genome-wide significance threshold (P < 5e-8) but does reach the suggestive threshold (P < 1e-5).

In the discovery cohort, five additional markers in linkage disequilibrium with rs10865291 (r-squared > 0.5) also reach suggestive significance. After genotype imputation, seven further SNPs in the same region reach suggestive significance. rs10865291 remains the single most significant marker in the region.
A genome-wide gene-based association test (VEGAS2) run on the discovery cohort ranks EFEMP1 as the top gene genome-wide, empirical P = 3.9e-5.

In the discovery cohort, 19 markers total reach the suggestive significance threshold, located in 10 distinct genomic regions genome-wide. The 2p16.1/EFEMP1 region is one of these ten regions. No marker anywhere in the discovery cohort reaches the genome-wide significance threshold.

A second, independent cohort of 156 patients with BA and other extrahepatic anomalies, plus 212 matched controls, was genotyped separately (different array, different phenotype definition than the discovery cohort) specifically to test the 2p16.1 region identified in the discovery cohort.

A meta-analysis combining the discovery cohort and the second, independent cohort was performed. Three highly correlated markers at 2p16.1 (rs10865291, rs6761893, rs727878, r-squared > 0.8) reach genome-wide significance in the meta-analysis, with rs6761893 the most significant (P = 3.39e-8). None of the other nine regions that had reached suggestive significance in the discovery cohort alone reach genome-wide significance in the meta-analysis.

EFEMP1 gene expression was measured in liver tissue from three groups: BA patients (n=5), patients with other cholestatic liver diseases (n=7), and non-cholestatic controls (n=5). Expression differed significantly across the three groups (one-way ANOVA, P = 0.007), with higher expression in both the BA group and the other-cholestatic-disease group compared to non-cholestatic controls. A separate, previously published dataset found EFEMP1 expression elevated 2.85-fold in BA patients compared to non-cholestatic controls.
